# Introduction {#sec-intro}

PLACEHOLDER — see `docs/01_SCOPE_AND_TAXONOMY.md` §1 for the argument this section
must carry: hybridisation is the field's dominant claim of novelty, and the marginal
benefit of hybridisation over a properly tuned base learner is almost never tested.

The review literature this study builds on is summarised in @fig-coverage. Prior
surveys catalogue where neural and hybrid methods have been applied
[@Yang2021research; @Gopalakrishnan2018learning; @Cao2020pavement]; two recent
contributions name the underlying problem without converting it into per-study
evidence [@Tamagusko2023learning; @MharziAlaoui2026algorithm].

## Information sources and search

Records were identified from OpenAlex, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and
Semantic Scholar, with backward and forward snowballing from the
`{python} len(reviews)` prior reviews listed in @tbl-reviews. The window runs from
1 January 2005 to 30 June 2026.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reviews
#| tbl-cap: "Prior reviews of artificial-intelligence methods in pavement engineering, with the territory each occupies."
from IPython.display import Markdown
lines = ["| Review | Year | Venue | Territory |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
for r in sorted(reviews, key=lambda x: int(x["year"])):
    first = r["authors"].split(";")[0].split(",")[0]
    extra = " et al." if ";" in r["authors"] else ""
    lines.append(f"| {first}{extra} | {r['year']} | {r['venue']} | {r['pavement_domain']} |")
Markdown("\n".join(lines))
```
